subject: typewriter
reasoning:
I'm planning a stylized, blocky typewriter model using the SDK, sized roughly 0.42m wide, 0.15m tall, 0.35m deep, with its base resting at y=0.

Since props need at least one joint to resolve parts correctly, I'll create a root joint called "body" at the origin so all parts attach to it by default. I'm sketching out the construction with boxes and cylinders for the main body and roller, considering simple color strings or paint patterns like a gradient for the top plate to keep it visually appealing without overcomplicating things.

I'm weighing whether to texture the keycaps with SVG letters, but since texture loading is asynchronous and the builder won't wait for it, I'll skip that risk and instead use solid key colors with maybe a gradient paint for the paper to add visual interest safely. Now I'm planning out the overall dimensions and orientation—keyboard facing forward toward the viewer, carriage and platen at the back, paper sticking out the top—starting with a width around 0.44 meters.

Now I'm sketching the main body components: a black housing box, cream-colored keys, a red accent detail, and a sloped keyboard tray extending forward from the main body.

Next I'm adding the carriage assembly — a rotated cylinder acting as the platen roller, positioned at the back top of the typewriter, plus thin rail boxes to support it and a paper sheet slab rising up behind the roller.

Writing paint function for text lines...

Now planning the keyboard keys layout, arranging rows of small key cap boxes across the deck at different z positions.

Adding feet cylinders at the corners, side knobs for ribbon spools, and a rod for the return lever...

Now I'm sketching a fan of thin rods arcing up from behind the keyboard toward the platen to represent the typebar basket, plus setting up the final export with a builder root and planning a colored logo panel on the body.

I'm working through the rod, paper, and platen geometry details—rotation parameters, tube radii, cylinder segments—then starting on the loop structure for generating the keys rows.

Still working out keyboard geometry...

Now I'm positioning the carriage housing and platen assembly at the back of the typewriter, sizing the arms that hold the platen roller and checking clearances against the body height so the arms support it properly above the deck.

Then I'm placing the paper as a thin tilted box behind the roller, working out the rotation so the top edge leans backward over the platen rather than forward, approximating how paper would feed through and curl over the top.

Now I'm writing a paint function for the paper surface that creates faint repeating horizontal text lines across the middle, giving it a typed-page look. I'm also adding a small red lever rod for an accent color, then sketching out the typebar fan as a series of rods arcing from the key area up toward the platen strike point.

I'm deciding the typebars are hidden beneath the deck anyway, so I'll skip drawing them since they wouldn't be visible. Instead I'm adding brass platen knobs at both ends, four rubber feet as small dark cylinders under the body corners, and starting to place a small logo detail on the front face of the typewriter body.

Now I'm settling on the color scheme: a dark body paired with a cream deck and pale keys for good contrast, deciding against adding painted key letters to keep things simple.

I'm adding a chrome strip along the front of the deck, then setting up the actual build code — creating a root body joint, using box and cylinder geometries for each part, applying rotation options where needed, and exporting the final metadata.
